 Aaron, I'm a big child, so the first part of your message made me laugh. 
 The Williams of Carlos Sainz slot in behind Fernando Alonso, more than three tenths off his fellow Spaniard. But now Aston Martin have a message for the two-time world champion. "Stop the car on track," he's told. 
 The red flag is out, and now Alonso is climbing safely out of the car. Lewis Hamilton had just gone quickest, with McLaren's Oscar Piastri dropping Alonso down to third.

 Mercedes lead the way published at 21:02 GMT 31 October 21:02 GMT 31 October 
 In the constructors' championship, Mercedes have a slim chance of securing the team title this weekend, but like Kimi Antonelli last week in Austin, the Silver Arrows need a lot to go their way to make that happen. 
 The leaders hold an 133-point advantage over second-placed Ferrari, with Red Bull now in third place and level with McLaren after Max Verstappen's run of podiums.

 Antonelli close to title win published at 20:58 GMT 31 October 20:58 GMT 31 October 
 Image source, Getty Images Pole position isn't a must for Kimi Antonelli in Mexico; all he has to do is keep his nose clean and finish inside the top 10 to be crowned champion. The Italian is 123 points clear of Mercedes team-mate George Russell and 124 free of Ferrari Lewis Hamilton. 
 Second place is still very much up grabs, with Hamilton, Max Verstappen and Charles Leclerc all chasing down Russell and separated by just nine points.

 Hirakawa replaces Ocon for Mexico City Grand Prix published at 20:55 GMT 31 October 20:55 GMT 31 October 
 Image source, Getty Images If you're just joining us tonight, you may have missed the news Esteban Ocon has been replaced by Ryo Hirakawa for the Mexico City Grand Prix. 
 Haas haven't given any more details as to why Ocon won't be driving, but the Frenchman did have an exchange with his race engineer Laura Mueller during second practice on Friday about tyre strategy. 
 Hirakawa drove Ocon's car during first practice yesterday, and this will be the Japanese driver's grand prix debut. 
 The 32-year-old finished 19th on the timesheets earlier, just above the Cadillac of Valtteri Bottas.

 Verstappen and Lawson set for grid drop published at 20:52 GMT 31 October 20:52 GMT 31 October 
 Keep an eye on Max Verstappen and Liam Lawson during tonight's qualifying session, as the two drivers have both been handed a one-place grid penalty for Sunday's race for their collision during yesterday's practice session. 
 After Sergio Perez's car troubles in third practice, the home driver will be desperate to get out track for qualifying, as tomorrow will be his 300th grand prix start. 
 36 13 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Norris leads Antonelli in FP3 published at 20:49 GMT 31 October 20:49 GMT 31 October 
 Image source, Getty Images Unless something disastrous happens during Kimi Antonelli's race on Sunday, reigning world champion Lando Norris will be handing over the title baton to the Italian at the chequered flag. But in third practice, the McLaren driver was able to pip the Mercedes man by the smallest of margins - 0.001 seconds to be exact. 
 Charles Leclerc, who was the driver to beat on Friday, was third quickest ahead of the other McLaren of Oscar Piastri and Red Bull's Max Verstappen, who had issues with his brakes late on in the session. 
 Lewis Hamilton, a winner here for Mercedes in 2019, was sixth, while George Russell, the man who is one point clear of Hamilton in second place in the standings, was seventh. 
 Verstappen's team-mate Isack Hadjar was eighth, with the two Racing Bulls of Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad in ninth and 10th. 
 Mexican driver Sergio Perez and Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto both failed to set a lap time in FP3, as engine problems limited their track running.

 Welcome back published at 20:45 GMT 31 October 20:45 GMT 31 October 
 Lorraine McKenna 
BBC Sport Journalist 
 Image source, Getty Images Hello again, folks. Who will take pole position for tomorrow's Mexico City Grand Prix, the second of this Americas triple-header? 
 We're at high altitude at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez and so far, Ferrari's Charles Leclerc has been quickest in two practice sessions, with Lando Norris finishing top in the final hour earlier on. 
 It was close between the top teams in third practice, so this should be an intriguing fight for pole position.
 Championship leader Kimi Antonelli is looking strong on the weekend he can become the new world champion with races remaining, while over at Haas, Esteban Ocon is nowhere to be seen, as the Frenchman has been replaced by Japanese reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa for the rest of the Mexican track action.
 24 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Norris fastest ahead of Antonelli in final practice published at 18:46 GMT 31 October 18:46 GMT 31 October 
 Andrew Benson 
BBC F1 correspondent 
 Image source, Getty Images McLaren’s Lando Norris pipped Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli to the fastest time in final practice on the weekend on which the world title is poised to change hands from the Briton to the Italian.
 Norris pipped Antonelli by just 0.001 seconds at the end of the last session before qualifying as both moved ahead of Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc, who was fastest on Friday but 0.117secs off on Saturday.
 Antonelli will become champion on Sunday as long as he does not lose more than 23 points to team-mate George Russell or 24 to Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton. The only way Antonelli can be prevented from winning the title is if Russell wins and he finishes lower than ninth, or Hamilton does and he is out of the points.
 McLaren’s Oscar Piastri was fourth fastest, 0.195secs off the pace, with Red Bull’s Max Verstappen 0.351secs behind Norris in fifth and ahead of Hamilton.
 Russell and Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar brought up the rear of the drivers from the top four teams, with Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad completing the top 10.
 News before practice was that Esteban Ocon has been dropped from his Haas seat for the rest of the weekend and replaced by reserve driver Roy Hirokawa . The Japanese was 19th in final practice, fourth places and 0.577secs behind team-mate Oliver Bearman.
 At the back, neither Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto or Cadillac’s Sergio Perez set a time as they suffered engine problems that required a power-unit change.

 Back for qualifying at 20:45 GMT published at 18:46 GMT 31 October 18:46 GMT 31 October 
 Is Lando Norris going to make a bid for pole position for tomorrow's 71-lap grand prix in Mexico? Or is the fight between Ferrari and young title leader Kimi Antonelli? 
 Mercedes' Antonelli doesn't have to book a spot on the front row for Sunday's race, as he only needs a top-nine finish to secure his maiden championship. But starting on pole for your date with destiny would be nice. 
 Right, if you want to head out trick-or-treating so you've got some sweets in for qualifying, do it now. 
 We'll be back up and running from 20:45 GMT. 
 Q1 is going green at 21:00. 
 See you shortly!

 Chequered flag published at 18:32 GMT 31 October 18:32 GMT 31 October 
 All the practice sessions are in the books in Mexico. 
 McLaren's Lando Norris tops the final hour of running with a time of 1:17.600 on the soft compound. 
 Champion in waiting Kimi Antonelli is second, only a fraction behind Norris, while Charles Leclerc is third on the timesheets. 
 The other McLaren of Oscar Piastri finishes fourth and Red Bull's Max Verstapen, who flagged problems with his brakes late on, ends his practice in fifth.
